capabilities: translate the current file, selection, or whole note into a new file
detect the language of selected text
translate in a customizable Translation View with automatic translation
switch between ten translation services via commands or context menus
extras: API keys are stored in plain text by default; translated text is sent to the selected service, and most services have free monthly character limits that may require a credit card at signup. Detailed documentation with tutorial videos is hosted separately.
motivation: The author says it started as a personal passion project and ballooned into something much bigger than intended.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to translate notes or selections or to detect their language via external translation services.

relations.evidence: This plugin makes use of full codefiles from the following projects: - FastText - Bergamot
Following projects were also referenced for writing functions, but adapted to fit the plugin's needs: - Obsidian-Translator

requires.name: account with the chosen translation service
Docker (Libre Translate) or a Bergamot binary for offline use

summary: Translation plugin that translates selected text, files, and a custom translation view through ten services including Google Translate, DeepL, Azure, and self-hosted options.
